ruling.recommended_action: Send to a Ryde human reviewer as a SAFE-1 rider-conduct case: record F4 verbatim as a threat of assault aimed at the driver, note the driver's statement (F6) that he kept driving and did not reply, confirm the complete timestamped chat (F5) and the clean system record (F1, F2: 8.5 km vs 8.5 km, 13.2 min vs 16.3 min), and take no fare or account action against either party in this referral.
ruling.reasoning: Case B-0045 is a driver-filed safety complaint. The complete, fully timestamped chat record [F5] contains exactly two lines: at 18:24 the driver wrote "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3] and the rider replied "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4]. Read in context, the rider's line is a threat of physical violence aimed at the driver — in substance intimidation of the other party, not a route or fare argument. Under SAFE-1, a threat, intimidation or abuse of any kind in the chat record sends the case to a person instead of an automatic ruling, so no fare or fee decision is made here.
ruling.escalation_reason: Driver-filed safety incident alleging a rider threat of physical violence; SAFE-1 requires a human reviewer, no automatic ruling.

rejected_claims.reason: The no-detour point is correct on the record (F1: 8.5 km vs 8.5 km optimal, +0.0 km; F2: 13.2 min vs 16.3 min), but RD-1/RD-2 have no work to do: with no off-route segment fact and no fare fact in this file there is no refundable amount to compute, and the trace limits this case to escalate under SAFE-1, so no fare outcome is issued.

RD-6 requires the case to be established against a party (RD-2 refund > 0 or an RD-1 violation recorded) before any account flag can follow, and NS-2 requires a failed no-show cancellation that did not occur here; both predicates are absent (F1, F2, F7, F8), so no flag is added — as the rider's own advocate accepts.

The driver's post-trip statement (F6) describing his own conduct is untested by any system record and cannot establish anything against the rider beyond what the chat already shows; it is preserved for the reviewer, not weighed as proof, and the case is decided on F3/F4 under SAFE-1.

Profile facts decide nothing on their own: the driver's clean record (F8) and the rider's history (F7) cannot establish or defeat the safety finding, which rests on the words in F4 read against F3 under SAFE-1.
